problem: Find the parametric equations of the line $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y-1}{4}=\frac{z+1}{3}.$
worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y-1}{4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(2,1,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨2,4,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+2t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}
$$
